items.title: Anthropic Commits Equity to Public Benefit (1 minute read)
items.snippet: Anthropic announced plans to allocate an initial 5% of its equity to a new Public Benefit Fund, with additional contributions tied to valuation growth. The fund will support initiatives such as addressing AI's economic and labor impacts.

items.title: OpenAI testing new "Aurora" GPT-Image model on Arena (3 minute read)
items.snippet: Three new model references briefly appeared in OpenAI's API and in blind arena tests this weekend. aurora-red-alpha, aurora-green-alpha, and aurora-blue-alpha appear to be image models and could possibly be GPT Image 3. In tests, red ran faster than green but was lower quality, while green was slower but looked better. Examples of images generated by the models are available in the article.

items.title: How AI Is Reshaping Anthropic's Workforce (17 minute read)
items.snippet: Anthropic reported a decline in junior technical hiring, with entry-level workers falling from 27% to 9% of technical hires since early 2025. Employees reported productivity gains from Claude, but increased AI output also shifted work toward supervising agents and made human attention a growing bottleneck.

items.title: How to Trust Your Coding Agents More (2 minute read)
items.snippet: Reliable coding agents require better code architecture, strong invariants, and automated verification rather than extensive prompting or human review. Analyze past agent mistakes and code reviews to redesign systems that prevent recurring failures by default.

items.title: Search & Fetch (8 minute read)
items.snippet: DeepSeek's Search and Fetch APIs give agents and RAG applications access to live web content. The Search API finds web pages for a query and returns structured results. The Fetch API retrieves a single web page and returns its content as Markdown. Both are raw JSON APIs. They use the same bearer authentication as the DeepSeek API.

It also reduces task execution time and output length, advancing the performance-cost Pareto frontier across multiple agent harnesses. items.title: How the Claude Code team does code review (18 minute read)
items.snippet: The Claude Code team has restructured its code review process to handle increased volume efficiently by automating most review stages. Key changes include continuous review, automated verifications, multi-layer checks before human intervention, and a tiered risk system for approvals.

items.title: Replit Switches Its Default AI Provider to OpenAI (3 minute read)
items.snippet: Replit replaced Anthropic with OpenAI as its preferred provider for Replit Agent, citing cost, performance, and partnership considerations. CEO Amjad Masad clarified that users could still select Claude and other supported models.

items.title: A benchmark map of the US economy (16 minute read)
items.snippet: The Benchmark Map is a project aimed at building a comprehensive, continuously updated resource for understanding AI capabilities across the economy. Initial findings suggest that 90% of American working hours are spent on tasks with little or no coverage from existing benchmarks. This makes it very hard to know how good AI models are at the work Americans actually do.

items.title: Claude reveals ECDSA curve origins (9 minute read)
items.snippet: Claude revealed the origins of ECDSA curve seeds, showing they were derived using a C library's lrand48 random number generator seeded with Unix timestamps, rather than hash algorithms or backdoors.

items.title: Qualcomm says AI labs want 100B-parameter models running on phones by 2028 (2 minute read)
items.snippet: AI companies want phones that run 100B-plus-parameter models continuously by 2028, and some are already starting to build their own phones.

items.title: Stripe survey: Four trends reshaping how SaaS platforms compete in the AI era
items.snippet: AI is creating more SaaS competition, and platforms are feeling the pressure. A Stripe survey of 200 platform leaders shows how they plan to evolve pricing, grow revenue, and retain customers.
